name: catharsis
quote: Glad I got that off my chest.
description: A perception of relief from negative feelings after having gone through a period of intense experience.
perceptions: I think it helped me feel better.
results: Perhaps you feel better for an extended period, or perhaps not.
examples: Expressing anger on a punching bag.

guidance.description: Despite being an ancient idea, there's debate amongst psychologists about if and how catharsis works for different situations, and whether it's a good approach to improving problems. The gist: (a) 'Letting out' anger doesn't work, and in fact just reinforces more anger. (b) Catharsis may work by letting you know that you're not alone, that others feel similarly and support you. (c) Or perhaps catharsis works by exposing repressed experiences. (d) Being pushed into reliving a traumatic state could trigger inner defenses.

variations.name: venting
variations.description: A sense that outwardly expressing something negative for a moment may relieve some stress.
perceptions: Letting myself express it may help relieve some pressure.
results: Perhaps the venting will help, or perhaps not.
examples: Cursing to yourself about how slowly the line is moving.
Making a sarcastic remark to the salesman about how prices have gone up.
Using a punching bag to express anger.

guidance.description: While letting your negative emotions out may feel good in the moment, science suggests it might make matters worse in the long run.

comparisons.description: 'Complaining' is one way to vent, but there are many non-verbal ways as well.

commentaries.quote: Art is a form of catharsis emotional release, purging, cleansing, purifying.
People believe that in letting things out, they’re getting rid of pent up emotions. In truth, other factors, such as social support, are what really provide that relief.
God, it was good to let go, let the tight mask fall off, and the bewildered, chaotic fragments pour out. It was the purge, the catharsis.

In some therapeutic modalities, catharsis is the key element to healing. The goal in such modalities is to dive deep into the experience, relive it once again and through this – release the pain you’re holding. In Internal Family Systems we actually don’t want the catharsis.
Catharsis is about cleansing and healing at one and the same time - healing memories and attitudes, healing the spirit and the heart.

For me, fiction isn't very cathartic. It can be a broad, long catharsis, but it's a whole different thing - whereas music is physical. Essentially, it goes in through your ear. Fiction is cerebral, necessarily. It can do emotional stuff. But they don't really compare - not for me.
Encouraging people to act out their anger makes them relive it in their bodies, strengthening the neural pathways for anger and making it easier to get angry the next time around.
Just scream! You vent, and the body just feels good after a good old yell.
